text: Welcome to your bistro! First, shop for today's cooking. Open Recipes in the top bar to see what each dish needs, then drag food from the shelves into your cart. Buy enough for at least one recipe, then check out.

Sort each new food into Green, Yellow or Red. Green foods are the everyday foundation and the only foods that build health. Yellow foods are ones customers are moving away from. Red foods are the ones to avoid. Flip a card to read its ingredients. Each new food you sort correctly gives back {maxDiscount} of what you paid for it. Answers are final once you submit.
Time to cook! Pick a recipe you have ingredients for. Faded recipes are missing something.

Drag one serving at a time from your pantry into the recipe's slots. A red outline means a slot still needs something. Drag a row out of a slot to put it back. For your first dish, fill every slot exactly, then press Review dish.

Your first dish is done! You used {ingredients}. Health changed by {healthDelta}, and it covered these Daily Dozen groups: {dailyDozen}. Only Green foods build health. Each Daily Dozen group a guest hasn't had before adds a little extra, so vary the plants you serve. From now on, you can also serve dishes that don't match the recipe, but guests will notice.

That guest felt a quick burst of energy, then a slump. A rush can feel good in the moment, but it doesn't mean the meal was good for them. Judge a meal by what's in it, not by how lively a guest seems afterwards.

A letter from the landlord: from tomorrow, rent of ${rent} is due every morning. You can only shop while you have money, so keep a little cushion. Busy evenings bring in takeaway income, and guests will soon start arriving with requests.

Money is running low, and tomorrow's rent could leave you unable to shop. Open Pantry, drag food you won't use onto SELL, then press Sell. Food that would spoil before you cook it is the best thing to sell.

From today, guests may ask for something, like Savory, Creamy or Crunchy. Each recipe shows what it answers. Answering a request delights a guest and grows your popularity; ignoring it costs a little. Health still comes only from the foods you choose. Comfort is answered by any dish with an appeal of {comfort} or more.

Your pantry couldn't make any recipe, so a local farmer brought a small crate of plain staples, enough for one simple dish. The farmer can only help once a day, so shop or sell spare food to get back on your feet.

You have {totalDays} days to make your bistro's name. Each day: shop, sort what's new, then cook for your guests. Rent starts on day {rentStart}, and guests bring requests from day {cravingsStart}. At the end, your popularity and the community's wellbeing decide how the story ends.

Popularity is how well known your bistro is. More guests come at {guestThresholds} popularity (up to {maxGuests}), and above {walkInThreshold}, walk-in customers buy takeaway every evening. Delighted guests, answered requests and tasty plates raise it; mismatched dishes and ignored requests lower it.

Guests pay you, plus tips, for every dish, and the market takes your money for food. From day {rentStart}, rent of ${rent} is due each morning. You can only shop while you have money, and ending deep in debt closes the bistro. Short on cash? Sell spare food from the Pantry.
